subject.title: fix: harden Mattermost slash callback auth

question: Should Mattermost native slash command registration fail closed for every non-HTTPS callback URL, including explicit operator-configured HTTP URLs?
rationale: Current main warns and continues for HTTP callbacks; the PR changes a token-bearing callback security boundary and can disable existing deployments, so automation cannot choose the upgrade policy alone.

options.title: Require HTTPS fail-closed after proof
options.body: Accept the breaking security hardening once live Mattermost proof and release-note-ready upgrade guidance show HTTPS succeeds and HTTP is refused before registration.

options.title: Preserve explicit HTTP compatibility
options.body: Keep warning/registration for explicit HTTP deployments and narrow the fail-closed behavior to derived or clearly unsafe callbacks until a staged policy is approved.

options.title: Pause for security design
options.body: Leave the linked issue open and replace this PR with a maintainer-sponsored design if neither immediate break nor compatibility preservation is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Require HTTPS fail-closed after proof
recommendation.body: Accept the breaking security hardening once live Mattermost proof and release-note-ready upgrade guidance show HTTPS succeeds and HTTP is refused before registration.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged callback validation refresh that owns the adjacent token-boundary behavior this PR extends.
